clue.text: Compulsory premarital reading matter that may be objected to

definitions.text: Compulsory premarital reading matter that may be objected to

parts.words: Compulsory premarital reading matter that may be objected to
parts.note: the notice of an intended wedding read out in church on three Sundays, at which anyone may raise an objection

explanation.surface: Something every engaged couple must have read aloud, which a stranger might challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Banns are the public church announcement of a planned marriage, inviting objections.

clue.text: Anne is hopping mad

indicators.note: hopping suggests jumping about, so the letters of the two words leap into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone called Anne is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hopping mad' reads as one idiom, but 'hopping' is the anagram signal on ANNE IS and 'mad' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad in the sense of out of one's mind is a synonym.

clue.text: Feeling of hunger affects lion and anteater

parts.note: a pang is a sharp feeling, as of hunger

indicators.note: affects is read as acts upon or alters, so the letters of the big cat are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hunger pangs bother a lion as well as an anteater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affects' is the anagram signal, read as alters; 'and' simply joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The pangolin is a scaly mammal that feeds on ants, often called a scaly anteater.

clue.text: The tube for below-surface travel

parts.note: reads like the London Underground, but describes a swimmer's breathing pipe used just beneath the water

explanation.surface: A description of the London Underground as a way to travel below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's underground railway; the real sense is a breathing tube for swimming face down below the water's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimmer's breathing pipe lets a person travel face down just under the water.

clue.text: Game that may leave one cold

definitions.meaning: a board game played with round counters on a chequered board
cold air currents through a room can chill a person

explanation.surface: A game that bores or fails to excite the player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave one cold' looks like 'fail to interest', but literally means a chilly current of air.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkers is called by this name in Britain; it is also the plural of a cold current of air.

clue.text: It may be thrust upon people in the Sergeants' Mess

definitions.text: It may be thrust upon people

indicators.note: mess is read as a verb, to jumble up, so the letters of the rank are scrambled

explanation.surface: Something forced on soldiers dining in the sergeants' mess hall.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sergeants' Mess is a dining room, but 'Mess' is the anagram signal on SERGEANTS. The definition echoes Shakespeare's Twelfth Night: 'some have greatness thrust upon them'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoting Twelfth Night, eminence is something some people have forced on them unasked.

clue.text: Keeps on, showing stamina in trouble

indicators.note: trouble is read as to disturb, so the letters of the two words are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone persists, displaying stamina while in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' looks like one phrase, but 'in' is part of the fodder and 'trouble' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep on is to continue or uphold, a synonym.

clue.text: Tour arranged around mid-April in Cornwall

indicators.note: around signals the rearranged letters going outside the other piece
arranged means the letters of the trip word are put in a new order
mid points to the middle letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: A tour organised in Cornwall for the middle of April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns TOUR into TURO, and 'around' puts R, the middle of APRIL, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Truro is the cathedral city and county town of Cornwall, the county at England's south-western tip.

clue.text: Area of land is left diminished by a foot

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: diminished by means made smaller by losing the following piece

parts.note: taken as written
FT is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: A plot of land that has been shortened by twelve inches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diminished by' removes FT (foot) from LEFT, leaving LE.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is a piece of land, and this word is a poetic name for one.

clue.text: What peace-makers try to do is put at risk

definitions.meaning: peacemakers try to stop people being cross, split as two words

explanation.surface: The aim of peace-makers is itself dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 3,5 it is what a peacemaker wants: to finish off fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil is to put in danger; as two words it means to stop the fury.

clue.text: Cry out-to the police?

definitions.meaning: to inform on someone to the police, slang

explanation.surface: A shout addressed to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill cry is a squeal, and in slang to squeal is to inform on a criminal.

clue.text: Circus performer to make an impression

definitions.meaning: an animal that balances balls on its nose in a circus
to press a stamp into wax

explanation.surface: A circus act trying to impress the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make an impression' looks like impressing an audience, but means stamping wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A performing marine mammal is a circus act, and to stamp wax is to press a mark into it.

clue.text: The plane might be a Jumbo

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: An aircraft could be a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' looks like a jumbo jet; it was the name of a famous zoo animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo was a celebrated London Zoo pachyderm, and the name is used for any big trunked beast.

clue.text: Difficult to make love other than on the grass

parts.note: difficult means hard
in the old sense, to make love is to woo or court

explanation.surface: It is hard to romance someone anywhere but on a lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make love' here is the old sense of wooing; the definition refers to a tennis surface that is not grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis surface of asphalt or concrete is an alternative to a grass lawn.

clue.text: Splitting hairs in divorce

definitions.meaning: the line where hair is combed in two directions

explanation.surface: Nit-picking during a divorce case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splitting hairs' means quibbling on the surface, but literally the line where hair divides.
explanation.definitionFit: A line combed in the hair divides it, and a separation of people is also so called.

clue.text: Spring a lock outside and make an entry unlawfully

indicators.note: outside means the hair piece goes round the spring piece

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Picking a lock to break in illegally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring a lock' suggests forcing a door open, but the spring is a mineral one and the lock is hair; 'outside' wraps the hair round the spring.
explanation.definitionFit: To go onto property without permission is to intrude unlawfully.

clue.text: Have the police party gone to the ship?

parts.note: a posse is a band of men called out to help a sheriff
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A question whether the officers have gone aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To own is to have, a synonym.

clue.text: Again, but for the last time presumably

definitions.meaning: the phrase used when asking for one final repeat

explanation.surface: Doing something again, supposedly for the final time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a further repetition, often said to suggest it will be the final one.

clue.text: Is to change state, but appears indifferent

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of the two short words

parts.note: CAL is an abbreviation of California, a US state

explanation.surface: A remark about switching states while seeming unmoved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' is the anagram signal on the two short words, giving STOI; 'state' is not the verb but California, a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unmoved by pain or pleasure is impassive, hence unconcerned.

clue.text: Disciple to stick by the New Testament

indicators.note: by means next to, so the scripture abbreviation sits beside the other piece

parts.note: to adhere is to stick

explanation.surface: A follower of Christ keeps close to the Gospels.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or supporter of a leader is a disciple.

clue.text: Handy fencing implement

parts.note: reads as a useful tool for putting up garden fences, but means a sword held in the hand for the sport

explanation.surface: A useful tool for erecting fences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fencing' suggests garden fences; 'Handy' is literal, held in the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sword used in the sport of fencing.

clue.text: What you have here, we hear, is for hanging a hammock

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is said aloud and the entry is a word with the same sound

parts.note: this line of the puzzle is itself a hint to the answer

explanation.surface: A sailor's remark about the cord on which a hammock hangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Clews are the cords by which a hammock is suspended, a nautical term.

clue.text: Fears loss of opener to slips

indicators.note: loss of opener means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: terrors are fears

explanation.surface: A cricket team worried about losing its opening batsman to fielders at slip.
explanation.walkthrough: Opener and slips suggest cricket (slip is a fielding position), but 'slips' means mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Slips are mistakes, synonyms.

clue.text: Sunderland docks

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Sunderland docks': no indicator or wordplay gives LANDS from Sunderland (only LAND is hidden), and searching the exact text found no fuller clue.

clue.text: Left in carriage and pair

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation goes inside the carriage word

parts.note: a coupé is a closed horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: Someone left in a horse-drawn carriage and pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage and pair' reads as one phrase, but 'pair' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Two together make a pair.

clue.text: I'm only human but never to be forgotten

parts.note: taken as written
a mortal is merely human

explanation.surface: A modest person who nonetheless will be remembered forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Undying fame means being remembered for all time.

clue.text: Get over feeling angry

explanation.surface: Getting past one's fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to go over, and one who is annoyed is so described.

clue.text: Just buying and selling

parts.note: reads as nothing but commerce, but just means equitable, describing ethical commerce paying producers properly

explanation.surface: Nothing but commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: The movement pays developing-world producers a decent price, so commerce is equitable.
